title: Jesus, to Thee I Now Can Fly
description: Jesus, to Thee I Now Can Fly in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 217. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, to thee I now can fly, On whom my help is laid: Op-pressed by sins, I lift my eye, And see the sha-dows fade.

lines: Jesus, to thee I now can fly,
On whom my help is laid:
Oppressed by sins, I lift my eye,
Believing on my Lord, I find
On thee alone my constant mind
Whate'er in me seems wise, or good,
I wash my garments in the blood
Jesus, my Strength, my Life, my Rest,
When faith in sight shall end.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
